# C · THE NUCLEAR CORRIDOR — refuted, and the screen it leaves

## ★★ C1 · The textbook family is REFUTED, structurally

    E = (N + 3/2) + β·ℓ(ℓ+1) − α·⟨L·S⟩

The ratio 4 is an **identity, not a coincidence** (R 1371, correcting 1368). For
two levels of one oscillator shell with Δℓ = 2, higher spin-antiparallel and
lower spin-parallel: Δ[ℓ(ℓ+1)] = 4ℓ+6, Δ⟨L·S⟩ = ℓ+3/2, ratio 4 for EVERY ℓ. The
constraint collapses to (ℓ+3/2)(4β + α) < 0 — it fixes the SIGN of one
combination. **SIX such pairs, three each way.** `corridor_identity.py`.

## ★★ C2 · The screen for replacements

R 1372: a candidate γ·T is admissible only if **ΔT is non-degenerate across those
six pairs**. A function of ℓ(ℓ+1) alone is the β slot; of ⟨L·S⟩ alone, the α
slot. **Six numbers screen a candidate before any fit.**

**NOT YET RUN** on the three named candidates: Woods–Saxon radial shape, a tensor
term, an ℓ-dependent effective mass. Also test the near-degenerate swaps both
ways — (2f7/2, 1h9/2) and (3p3/2, 2f5/2) — a form surviving either is robust.

---

# D · CAPTURE — the route now works

## ★★ D1 · The route

**The person pastes a URL; Claude fetches it live.** Established 2026-08-10 after
three rounds of generated tables failed verification. Nothing is transcribed by
anyone. Generated data failed on: ragged row counts, absent Ground-Shells column,
0.2–11% energy errors, and smoothed-away shell closures.

## ★★ D2 · The ionisation ladders — 15 of 108, +H,He,Li complete

    isoelectronic  11/11    the walk  106/106
    ionisation     ~15/108  ← this      isotopic  1 rung traced (R 1381)

    ie.pl?spectra=K-Kr+I-III&units=0&format=1&at_num_out=on&sp_name_out=on
      &ion_charge_out=on&seq_out=on&shells_out=on&level_out=on&e_out=0&unc_out=on

**K–Kr is the one that matters** — the whole 3d block, where ns/(n−1)d
competition lives, and it carries Ca I/II/III for A3. Then Rb–Xe, Cs–Rn, Fr–Ds.
Charge > 10 is IMPROBABLE (S.status) so I–XI suffices: ~1,170 rows not 6,027.

## ★ D3 · Theodosiou, Inokuti & Manson 1986 — the wholesale test

At. Data Nucl. Data Tables **35**, 473 (1986). Asymptotic quantum defects for s,
p, d, f across ALL ionisation stages of ALL ions with Z ≤ 50 — ~5,100
Hartree–Slater values against the compendium's 4,200. **Would replace R 1202's
standing weakness** (four of seven far anchors are theoretical) with thousands of
reference points.

## ★ D4 · AME2020 — CITED AND NOT HELD

`mathreg.py` and `indices.py` both cite it; no mass data in the restore point, so
**E.nuclide = 9 cannot be reproduced**. REPRODUCTION checks that the build runs,
not that its inputs are present. Same class of fault as R 1373.

## ★ D5 · Collection, what remains

**1,419 extractable cells** not yet measured — not 101,000. The Z × charge face is
the largest source of looseness at 1,935 admitted cells; the index holds 70 of
182 element–charge pairs. Of 112 missing pairs, closed-shell cores are genuine
gaps; **open-shell cores are not gaps at all** — levels published, no defect
extractable (R 1180).

---

# E · THE CHANNEL EQUATION — what it still gets wrong

    δ = a·p^e(Nₑ)·Nₑ^k·ln(c+1)/c        p > 0
    δ = h·C(Z)·((Nₑ−1)/Nₑ)·Nₑ^k·ln(c+1)/c   p = 0
    a = 0.3772 · e(Nₑ) = 0.8297 − 0.0900 ln Nₑ · k = 0.4942 · h = 0.5415
    284 channels, Z 2–90 · rms 0.1610 · R² 0.9741 · Pauli bound 328/328

## ★ E1 · The hydrogenic zero is ALGEBRAIC, not a prediction

At Nₑ = 1 the (Nₑ−1)/Nₑ factor vanishes for every charge and every C(Z). No
parameter can move it, so it is a tautology of the form rather than a test the
data passes. `hydrogenic_test.py`.

## ★ E2 · The relativistic wall, now on THREE objects

    hydrogenic ionisation, Z=92   +14.5% above Z²R
    Moseley KL3, Z=92             +14.2% above the linear law
    Kα doublet, Z≥70              +16% above C(Z−σ)⁴

Same electron, same shell, three independent measurements. **The equation is
non-relativistic — this is a DOMAIN statement, not a failure.**

## ★ E3 · Sr II and Ti IV share a signature

Low at s, p, d and high at f, growing with Nₑ — 0.33 at Nₑ=19, 0.70 at Nₑ=37.
The ℓ-dependence is not a linear coefficient: nearly flat across s, p, d, then a
cliff at f.

## ★ E4 · The polarisation floor is gone

The Janet term replaced it, so both f channels of the held-out species come out
at exactly zero where they measure 0.062 and 0.077. *Collapse dominates above the
boundary and polarisation below it; the equation has only one.*

## ★ E5 · The residual bow

0.93 at Nₑ 2–6, 1.10 at 6–15, 1.02 at 15–32, 0.89 at 32–60. Survived every form
tried. **Carcassés & González flag the same domain**, Phys. Rev. A 80 (2009)
024502 — E_ioniz = Z²N^(−2/3)g(N/Z), failing for neutrals.

---

# F · THE ARTEFACT PASS — see ARTEFACT-PASS.md

## ★★ F1 · Registers 1249–1381 · what has and has not landed

**Landed 2026-08-10**: the corridor identity and six-pair screen; Λ_xray and the
isotopic null in the Mathematical Compendium's authored tail; four new lines in
*what this work introduces*; the Löwdin reclassification in HANDOFF.

**Not landed**: the Kα doublet non-reduction (B1); the Index of Indices has no
Λ_xray entry and its §IX still reads *thirteen of fourteen close*; the Spectra
Compendium still wants the session's captures folded into `COORDINATES.tsv`.

## ★ F2 · The book owes two chapters

The Löwdin solution, and the three-body problem. **Nothing is written until both
a target and a solution exist** — R 1359 records the chapter that was written,
audited and CUT for claiming the problem factorises because there is no third
pair, which is false.

## ★ F3 · The compendium tail is AUTHORED, not generated

R 1373. `COMPENDIUM-TAIL.md` now holds it and `compendium.py` appends it; the
rebuild is verified idempotent. **Any future authored region must go the same
way** or the next rebuild eats it.

---

# G · UNFINISHED OBJECTS — two, both diagnosed

## ★ G1 · M.C2 — half-sided modular inclusion on a non-expanding horizon

OPEN on the GEOMETRIC route only — Sorce 2024 closes it by construction, since a
geometric modular flow needs a conformal Killing field. **The algebraic route is
not blocked.** The obstruction is in the corner edge modes, and it bottoms out at
POSITIVITY of the null translation generator, which Hadamard does not imply —
microlocal vs global spectral. R 1018–1022, 1038–1042.

## ★ G2 · Q.exch — the exchange factor, WITHDRAWN

The fitted sign is opposite to the measured one (R 1168). A uniform s can only
give 0/66 or 66/66 and the data says 55/66. **Needs an ℓ-dependent exchange
term** — Q.bound already carries the orbital count p the overlap should follow.

---

# H · THE CYPHER AUDIT — open items

**Three standing order/analysis contradictions on Λ_spectra**, named and not
adjudicated (R 1171): δ falls with ℓ (194/205 vs 102/205); triplet exceeds
singlet (55/66 vs 33/66); δ falls along a sequence (89/143 vs 135/143).

**Five language/index pairs never run**: Λ_spectra in geometry, algebra,
information and statistics; Λ_α in analysis. *The cypher's agreement is
established on Λ's 976 cells and asserted everywhere else.*

**Two operators still missing**: algebra's Gröbner basis needs a proper
Buchberger–Möller construction rather than the regularity proxy; information's
E_bits exists for Λ only.

---

# I · THE METHOD — protocols, rules, principles

## The protocols are CODE. Run them.

    domain_protocol.py   four questions before any fit. BLOCKS POOLING.
    chem_index.py        routes a residual to its property and class
    t_index.py           Λ_t, the corridor position on (ℓ, n)
    ladder_index.py      superseded by ladder_index2.py — still carries the
                         WITHDRAWN `state` axis (R 1356). NEEDS CORRECTING.
    distinguished_n.py   the magic sequences of four many-body systems
    nuclear_corridor.py  the refutation · corridor_identity.py the identity
    xray_index.py        Λ_xray · isotopic_null.py the null computation
    ground.py            108 observed neutral ground configurations

## The one microscope

**ℛ is the only lens.** When a piece verifies, ask WHERE ELSE THIS EXACT OBJECT
APPEARS. ℓ(ℓ+1) is one object seen six times. **Read orderings from a source;
never compute or recall them.**

## The rules, accumulated

Lock what is measured · one thing at a time · per element, not pooled · charge is
one symbol in three positions · evidence is not an object axis · calibrate on one
atom · **the neutral is not the table** · never fit across a language boundary ·
a law holding atom-by-atom need not hold as a walk · compendia answer, they do
not argue · figures removed must have their data represented another way ·
**do not invent a cell or a column — reshuffle until it fits or one cell remains**
(2026-08-10) · **an index needs THREE axes, never two** (K.three, R 1175) ·
**E = 0 is informative only where refusal was possible.**

## The seventeen mechanisms

`mech_audit`. Not repeated here.

    B.coll   |ψ(0)|² ∝ ν⁻³, same cell as the level spacing
    B.rank1  that family factorises EXACTLY, 2nd singular value 1.8e−14

**One measured constant + a derived scaling = δ per channel.** If it holds it is
the first time an operator-side cell in this work has been crossed rather than
described. HELD: `XRAY-KL3.tsv`, `XRAY-KL2.tsv`.

## ★★ A2 · Λ_spectra's closure — it lacks n

R 1341 names the cause. Λ_ryd holds the n-dependence Λ_spectra discards
(δ₀, δ₂, δ₄). The merged index **(Z, c, n, ℓ, 2S+1)** supplies it. This is the
index A1's output must populate.

## ★★ A3 · a is a(period, block, c) — every bracket is the c = 1 slice

At Nₑ = 20 the ordering reverses across three charges with E(3d²) − E(4s²)
swinging 17 eV. Λ_var said so before the brackets were built.
**Now feedable**: `LADDER-H-Ar-I-III.tsv` holds c = 0,1,2 for Z 1–18. The K–Kr
block is the one that matters (see D2) — Z 1–18 has no ns/(n−1)d competition.

# B · THE INDEXES

## ★★ B1 · Λ_xray — new, closed, partially valued

33 dipole lines → **9 cells** on Δn × Δℓ × jtype_hole, E = 0. `xray_index.py`.
Built from Λ's own transition alphabet + EM.map + T.a12, no new data.

**Language profile settled** (R 1379): unlike Λ_cross it has BOTH a statistics
language (pairwise marginals recover all 9) and an analysis language (Moseley,
R² = 0.998). Λ_cross remains the only integer object.

**Open — the coupling rung does not reduce.** The Kα doublet is measured across
85 unblended elements and no two-parameter form in Λ's vocabulary fits it:
(Z − σ)⁴ leaves 20% scatter and a ratio drifting 0.71 → 1.16 across the table.
Report the measurement, not a fit. NOT yet written to any artefact.

**Wanted**: L1M2, L1M3, L2M1, L2M4, L3M1, L3M4, L3M5 — the L-shell lines, which
test whether the nine types hold at a second depth.

## ★★ B2 · Λ_ladder — six species + the state family

`ladder_index2.py`. E = 1 on seat × kind × Zcross, 7 cells, defect at
**subvalence**, two candidates (counting-across-elements = Moseley;
coupling-within = the doublet). **Recompute with both X-ray ladders in** — that
is what resolves the E = 1 or makes it a genuine singleton.

Still open: whether isoelectronic/the walk and isotonic/isobaric sharing cells
is a fault or a finding (one object seen twice).

## ★ B3 · Λ_t — three empty cells, and two may be unreachable

7p, 6d, 7d. **ASD stops at Ds (Z = 110)**, and 7p needs Z ≥ 113. So 6d is
reachable (Ac, Th, Rf–Ds) and 7p/7d probably are not — which would make them
REAL ABSENCES rather than collection gaps, the R 1180 distinction.

## ★ B4 · Λ_ladder's own arithmetic — settled, recorded

Z = Nₑ + c − 1 leaves two of three independent; no ladder varies Z alone.
A = Z + N does the same on the nuclear side. R 1374.

---

# C · THE NUCLEAR CORRIDOR — refuted, and the screen it leaves

## ★★ C1 · The textbook family is REFUTED, structurally

    E = (N + 3/2) + β·ℓ(ℓ+1) − α·⟨L·S⟩

The ratio 4 is an **identity, not a coincidence** (R 1371, correcting 1368). For
two levels of one oscillator shell with Δℓ = 2, higher spin-antiparallel and
lower spin-parallel: Δ[ℓ(ℓ+1)] = 4ℓ+6, Δ⟨L·S⟩ = ℓ+3/2, ratio 4 for EVERY ℓ. The
constraint collapses to (ℓ+3/2)(4β + α) < 0 — it fixes the SIGN of one
combination. **SIX such pairs, three each way.** `corridor_identity.py`.

## ★★ C2 · The screen for replacements

R 1372: a candidate γ·T is admissible only if **ΔT is non-degenerate across those
six pairs**. A function of ℓ(ℓ+1) alone is the β slot; of ⟨L·S⟩ alone, the α
slot. **Six numbers screen a candidate before any fit.**

**NOT YET RUN** on the three named candidates: Woods–Saxon radial shape, a tensor
term, an ℓ-dependent effective mass. Also test the near-degenerate swaps both
ways — (2f7/2, 1h9/2) and (3p3/2, 2f5/2) — a form surviving either is robust.

# D · CAPTURE — the route now works

## ★★ D1 · The route

**The person pastes a URL; Claude fetches it live.** Established 2026-08-10 after
three rounds of generated tables failed verification. Nothing is transcribed by
anyone. Generated data failed on: ragged row counts, absent Ground-Shells column,
0.2–11% energy errors, and smoothed-away shell closures.

    isoelectronic  11/11    the walk  106/106
    ionisation     ~15/108  ← this      isotopic  1 rung traced (R 1381)

    ie.pl?spectra=K-Kr+I-III&units=0&format=1&at_num_out=on&sp_name_out=on
      &ion_charge_out=on&seq_out=on&shells_out=on&level_out=on&e_out=0&unc_out=on

**K–Kr is the one that matters** — the whole 3d block, where ns/(n−1)d
competition lives, and it carries Ca I/II/III for A3. Then Rb–Xe, Cs–Rn, Fr–Ds.
Charge > 10 is IMPROBABLE (S.status) so I–XI suffices: ~1,170 rows not 6,027.

## ★ D3 · Theodosiou, Inokuti & Manson 1986 — the wholesale test

At. Data Nucl. Data Tables **35**, 473 (1986). Asymptotic quantum defects for s,
p, d, f across ALL ionisation stages of ALL ions with Z ≤ 50 — ~5,100
Hartree–Slater values against the compendium's 4,200. **Would replace R 1202's
standing weakness** (four of seven far anchors are theoretical) with thousands of
reference points.

`mathreg.py` and `indices.py` both cite it; no mass data in the restore point, so
**E.nuclide = 9 cannot be reproduced**. REPRODUCTION checks that the build runs,
not that its inputs are present. Same class of fault as R 1373.

**1,419 extractable cells** not yet measured — not 101,000. The Z × charge face is
the largest source of looseness at 1,935 admitted cells; the index holds 70 of
182 element–charge pairs. Of 112 missing pairs, closed-shell cores are genuine
gaps; **open-shell cores are not gaps at all** — levels published, no defect
extractable (R 1180).

    δ = a·p^e(Nₑ)·Nₑ^k·ln(c+1)/c        p > 0

    a = 0.3772 · e(Nₑ) = 0.8297 − 0.0900 ln Nₑ · k = 0.4942 · h = 0.5415
    284 channels, Z 2–90 · rms 0.1610 · R² 0.9741 · Pauli bound 328/328

## ★ E1 · The hydrogenic zero is ALGEBRAIC, not a prediction

At Nₑ = 1 the (Nₑ−1)/Nₑ factor vanishes for every charge and every C(Z). No
parameter can move it, so it is a tautology of the form rather than a test the
data passes. `hydrogenic_test.py`.

    hydrogenic ionisation, Z=92   +14.5% above Z²R
    Moseley KL3, Z=92             +14.2% above the linear law
    Kα doublet, Z≥70              +16% above C(Z−σ)⁴

Same electron, same shell, three independent measurements. **The equation is
non-relativistic — this is a DOMAIN statement, not a failure.**

Low at s, p, d and high at f, growing with Nₑ — 0.33 at Nₑ=19, 0.70 at Nₑ=37.

The Janet term replaced it, so both f channels of the held-out species come out

boundary and polarisation below it; the equation has only one.*

0.93 at Nₑ 2–6, 1.10 at 6–15, 1.02 at 15–32, 0.89 at 32–60. Survived every form
tried. **Carcassés & González flag the same domain**, Phys. Rev. A 80 (2009)
024502 — E_ioniz = Z²N^(−2/3)g(N/Z), failing for neutrals.

OPEN on the GEOMETRIC route only — Sorce 2024 closes it by construction, since a
geometric modular flow needs a conformal Killing field. **The algebraic route is
not blocked.** The obstruction is in the corner edge modes, and it bottoms out at
POSITIVITY of the null translation generator, which Hadamard does not imply —
microlocal vs global spectral. R 1018–1022, 1038–1042.

## ★ G2 · Q.exch — the exchange factor, WITHDRAWN

The fitted sign is opposite to the measured one (R 1168). A uniform s can only
give 0/66 or 66/66 and the data says 55/66. **Needs an ℓ-dependent exchange
term** — Q.bound already carries the orbital count p the overlap should follow.

---

# H · THE CYPHER AUDIT — open items

**Three standing order/analysis contradictions on Λ_spectra**, named and not
adjudicated (R 1171): δ falls with ℓ (194/205 vs 102/205); triplet exceeds
singlet (55/66 vs 33/66); δ falls along a sequence (89/143 vs 135/143).

**Five language/index pairs never run**: Λ_spectra in geometry, algebra,
information and statistics; Λ_α in analysis. *The cypher's agreement is

## The one microscope

**ℛ is the only lens.** When a piece verifies, ask WHERE ELSE THIS EXACT OBJECT
APPEARS. ℓ(ℓ+1) is one object seen six times. **Read orderings from a source;
never compute or recall them.**

## The rules, accumulated

Lock what is measured · one thing at a time · per element, not pooled · charge is
one symbol in three positions · evidence is not an object axis · calibrate on one
atom · **the neutral is not the table** · never fit across a language boundary ·
a law holding atom-by-atom need not hold as a walk · compendia answer, they do
not argue · figures removed must have their data represented another way ·
**do not invent a cell or a column — reshuffle until it fits or one cell remains**
(2026-08-10) · **an index needs THREE axes, never two** (K.three, R 1175) ·
**E = 0 is informative only where refusal was possible.**

Carried in `MECHANISMS.md` and cross-checked against `mathreg.py` by

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""contingency.py -- the check that must pass before any check is reported.

THE ERROR THIS EXISTS TO STOP

A check that cannot fail is not evidence. It passes, it is quoted beside
quantities the data does constrain, and it reads as confirmation. Four instances,
found separately and never connected until register 1383:

  · Q.final's HYDROGENIC ZERO. "hydrogenic output EXACTLY zero" sat among the fit
    statistics, between the rms and the Pauli bound. At Ne = 1 the factor
    (Ne-1)/Ne vanishes identically, for every charge and every C(Z). No parameter
    can move it and no data can confirm it. Register 1382.

  · B.brk, THE TRIVIAL BRACKET. "measured at 789 of 789 interior cells -- and it
    is the TRIVIAL bracket, which cannot fail." Registers 797, 830. The work
    caught this one and annotated it, which is why it is a model rather than a
    fault.

  · EM.image, VACUOUS CLOSURE. E = 0 because the image is a complete rectangle.
    "the one closure in this work that certifies nothing."

  · Lambda_ladder at FOUR CELLS. E = 0 with `fixes` injective on the ladders: 0
    of 60 comparable arrangements could refuse anything. The zero was forced, not
    measured. Registers 1374, 1375.

  · and the toolchain form: REPRODUCTION checks the build RUNS, not that it
    ROUND-TRIPS, so it passed while silently discarding 6,659 characters.
    Register 1373.

WHY THE EXISTING AUDITS DO NOT CATCH IT

MEASURE recomputes a stated value against the register and confirms it is right.
A quantity that is zero by construction recomputes to zero every time, so MEASURE
passes. REPRODUCTION confirms the build completes. Neither asks the prior
question: COULD THIS HAVE COME OUT OTHERWISE?

That question is not about the value. It is about the SPACE the value was drawn
from. A check has content exactly when the admissible space contains a neighbour
that fails it.

THE PROTOCOL

Before any check is reported as evidence, answer these four. If any answer is
wrong, the check is reported as STRUCTURAL and not as a result.

  1 WITNESS    Exhibit one admissible neighbour for which this check FAILS.
               Not a hypothetical -- construct it. If no such object exists in
               the admissible space, the check is FORCED.

  2 SPACE      What is the admissible space, stated before the check was run?
               If it was chosen after seeing the result, the witness is not
               independent and the check does not count.

  3 RATE       Over that space, what fraction of comparable objects FAIL? Report
               it beside the result. Near 0% means forced; near 100% means the
               check is trivially satisfied by nothing and the space is wrong.

  4 VANISHING  Does any factor, term or coordinate in the check vanish, saturate
               or become constant at the tested point? If so the check is about
               the remaining factors only, and must say which.

REPORTING RULE

A forced check is not deleted -- it is LABELLED. "E = 0, forced at four cells"
and "E = 0, earned: 76% of comparable arrangements refuse" are different claims
and must read differently. The label goes beside the number, in the same
sentence, exactly as B.brk carries "which cannot fail".
"""
import random
from itertools import product, permutations


def opR(X, d):
    X = set(X); vals = [sorted({x[i] for x in X}) for i in range(d)]
    def env(i, j):
        m = {}
        for x in X: m[x[j]] = max(m.get(x[j], -10**9), x[i])
        b, o = -10**9, {}
        for t in sorted(m): b = max(b, m[t]); o[t] = b
        return o
    phi = {(i, j): env(i, j) for i in range(d) for j in range(d) if i != j}
    return {x for x in product(*vals)
            if all(x[i] <= phi[(i,j)][x[j]] for i in range(d) for j in range(d) if i != j)}


def minE(cells, axes):
    b = None
    for p in product(*[permutations(range(a)) for a in axes]):
        cs = {tuple(p[i].index(x[i]) for i in range(len(axes))) for x in cells}
        E = len(opR(cs, len(axes))) - len(cs)
        b = E if b is None else min(b, E)
        if b == 0: return 0
    return b


def contingency_rate(cells, axes, trials=200, seed=0):
    """QUESTION 3 for a closure claim: over random cell sets of the SAME size on
    the SAME grid, what fraction can refuse anything?  Near 0 means E = 0 was
    forced by the shape and carries no information."""
    pool = [c for c in product(*[range(a) for a in axes])]
    n = len(cells); fails = tot = 0
    for s in range(trials):
        c = set(random.Random(seed + s).sample(pool, n))
        tot += 1
        if minE(c, axes) > 0: fails += 1
    return fails / tot


def label(E, rate):
    """The reporting rule, as a string to be carried beside the number."""
    if E > 0:
        return f"E = {E}, a defect ({100*rate:.0f}% of comparable sets also refuse)"
    if rate < 0.10:
        return f"E = 0, FORCED — only {100*rate:.0f}% of comparable sets could refuse"
    if rate < 0.25:
        return f"E = 0, WEAK — {100*rate:.0f}% of comparable sets could refuse"
    return f"E = 0, EARNED — {100*rate:.0f}% of comparable sets do refuse"


def vanishing(fn, point, names):
    """QUESTION 4: report which named factors vanish or saturate at the tested
    point. fn returns a dict name -> factor value."""
    f = fn(point)
    return {k: v for k, v in f.items() if v == 0 or v == 1}


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print(__doc__.split("THE PROTOCOL")[1].split("REPORTING RULE")[0].strip())
    print("\n" + "=" * 66)
    print("  THE PROTOCOL APPLIED TO THE FOUR KNOWN CASES\n")

    # 1 · Lambda_ladder at four cells vs six -- the closure form
    four = {(0,3,1),(1,3,1),(2,2,1),(3,0,0)}
    r4 = contingency_rate(four, [4,4,2], trials=60)
    print(f"  Λ_ladder, 4 cells, `fixes` injective : {label(minE(four,[4,4,2]), r4)}")

    six = {(3,2,0),(2,2,0),(1,1,0),(1,0,1),(0,0,1),(4,0,1)}
    r6 = contingency_rate(six, [5,3,2], trials=60)
    print(f"  Λ_ladder, 6 cells                    : {label(minE(six,[5,3,2]), r6)}")

    # 2 · Q.final's hydrogenic zero -- the vanishing form
    from math import log
    def qfinal_factors(pt):
        Ne, c = pt
        return {"(Ne-1)/Ne": (Ne - 1) / Ne, "Ne^k": Ne ** 0.4942,
                "ln(c+1)/c": log(c + 1) / c, "C(Z)": 1.0}
    v = vanishing(qfinal_factors, (1, 5), None)
    print(f"\n  Q.final at Ne = 1, c = 5 — factors that vanish or saturate:")
    for k, x in v.items():
        print(f"      {k:<12} = {x}")
    print("      -> the check is about the REMAINING factors only, and there")
    print("         are none. FORCED. Report as structural. (R 1382)")

    print("\n  B.brk, the trivial bracket : already labelled 'which cannot fail'")
    print("  EM.image                   : already labelled 'E = 0 vacuously'")
    print("\n  Those two are the MODEL. The protocol generalises their annotation.")

content.text:
**Built and registered as 1383.** `contingency.py`, joining `domain_protocol.py` as a gate rather than an audit — it runs before a check is reported, not on every build.

Four questions:

**WITNESS** — exhibit one admissible neighbour for which the check *fails*. Constructed, not hypothesised. If none exists, the check is forced.
**SPACE** — state the admissible set before running. Chosen afterwards, the witness isn't independent.
**RATE** — what fraction of comparable objects fail. Reported beside the result.
**VANISHING** — does any factor vanish or saturate at the tested point? If so the check concerns only the factors that remain.

The reporting rule is the part that matters: **a forced check is labelled, not deleted.** "E = 0, forced at four cells" and "E = 0, earned, 76% of comparable arrangements refuse" are different claims and must read differently.

And I'd flag that this isn't a new invention so much as a generalisation. B.brk already carries *"the TRIVIAL bracket, which cannot fail"* and EM.image carries *"E = 0 vacuously"* — the annotation existed twice, correctly written, and was never connected or made a requirement. Those two are the model.

Applied to the known cases:

| claim | verdict |
|---|---|
| Λ_ladder, 4 cells, `fixes` injective | **E = 0, FORCED** — 2% of admissible sets could refuse |
| Λ_ladder, 6 cells | **E = 0, EARNED** — 83% do refuse |
| Q.final at Nₑ = 1 | **FORCED** — (Nₑ−1)/Nₑ = 0, Nₑ^k = 1, C(Z) = 1; nothing remains |

One thing worth keeping. The protocol caught an error in its own first demonstration — it scored the four-cell case at 28% by sampling arbitrary cell sets, when a ladder is named by what it fixes and the space is row-injective. Restricted properly, 2%. So **RATE without SPACE is meaningless**, and that was question 2 failing on the protocol's own worked example. I've written that into the docstring and the register rather than quietly fixing it, since it's the most likely way the protocol gets misused.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""ladder_index.py -- Lambda_ladder, the index of the ladders themselves.

A ladder is a walk holding something fixed and varying the rest. Every result in
the Loewdin work came from one, and until register 1356 they were never indexed
as objects in their own right.

SUPERSEDES the version that carried `state` -- complete/partial/none -- on an
axis. That is the observer on an object axis, the fault that killed `standing` in
Lambda_const, `origin` in Lambda_var and `kind` in Lambda_phys. Register 1356
withdrew it; the code kept printing it until register 1384. It also absorbs
ladder_index2.py, which is now deleted: two scripts for one index is the same
class of hazard.

THE TWO RELATIONS

    Z = Ne + c - 1          the electronic relation, on Lambda
    A = Z + N               the nuclear relation, on the nuclide chart

Each is ONE linear relation on three named quantities, so fixing each quantity in
turn gives three ladders, and six in all. Register 1374. The nuclear three are
not a single "isotopic" direction; that undercount is what 1356 carried.

THE SECOND FAMILY

A SPECIES ladder varies which atom or ion. A STATE ladder fixes the species
entirely and varies which level of it. The work propagates along two of these
already -- the Rydberg series in n, and P.lcollapse in l, whose step ratio A.S
measures at 1.416 over 62 pairs -- without ever indexing them as ladders.

WHY THE OLD ANSWER WAS EMPTY

At four ladders `fixes` is injective on them by construction: a ladder IS named
by what it holds fixed. One cell per row, and the ordering that monotonises it
always exists, so E = 0 was FORCED -- 2% of admissible arrangements could refuse.
At six, ionisation and isotopic BOTH fix Z, `fixes` stops individuating, and the
zero becomes earnable. Registers 1374, 1375; contingency.py.
"""
from itertools import product, permutations

FAMILY = ["species", "state"]
SEAT   = ["nucleus", "core", "subvalence", "valence", "the aggregate"]
KIND   = ["counting", "coupling"]          # T.dich -- a proved dichotomy
ZCROSS = ["within one element", "across elements"]   # K.zcross

#  name                    family seat kind zcross   what it fixes / status
LAD = [
 ("isoelectronic",            0, 3, 0, 1, "fixes Ne        · 11 of 11"),
 ("the walk",                 0, 3, 0, 1, "fixes c         · 106 of 106"),
 ("ionisation",               0, 2, 0, 0, "fixes Z         · 15 of 108 (+H,He,Li)"),
 ("isotopic",                 0, 0, 0, 0, "fixes Z,Ne,c    · 1 rung traced, R 1381"),
 ("isotonic",                 0, 0, 0, 1, "fixes N         · NEW R 1374, untraced"),

I need to be direct about what happened here, because it's the most serious thing today.

**I destroyed a held artefact while testing for exactly that failure.** `physics.py` writes PHYSICS.md in place rather than to stdout, so my diff test — running the generator and comparing — regenerated the file over the original and deleted its authored Λ_chem section, 7,242 characters. I recovered it intact from `restore-point-1_6d.tar.gz`, cut twenty minutes earlier. Without that backup the loss would have been permanent and silent.

That is the argument for the backup you agreed to at the start of this stretch, made concrete within the hour.

**The finding, though, is larger than expected.** Three of five generated artefacts had an undeclared hand-authored region:

| artefact | authored region | round-trips now |
|---|---|---|
| COMPENDIUM.md | 6,659 chars, the Löwdin tail | yes |
| INDICES.md | 12,695 chars, section IX | yes |
| PHYSICS.md | 7,242 chars, Λ_chem | yes |
| SPECTRA.md | — | yes |
| REGISTER.md | — | yes |

Not one exception. A majority. And the in-place writer is the dangerous form — the stdout writers merely produce a short file, which a diff catches harmlessly, while the in-place writer destroys the evidence during the very test run to look for it.

So `physics.py` got one thing the other two didn't need: **if `PHYSICS-TAIL.md` is absent it now exits non-zero and writes nothing.** A generator that cannot produce its whole output must refuse to produce part of it. Rebuild verified byte-identical to the restore point.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""roundtrip.py -- the check that a GENERATED artefact regenerates itself.

THE ERROR THIS EXISTS TO STOP

Three of the five generated artefacts carried a hand-authored region that no
generator wrote, so every rebuild silently discarded it:

    COMPENDIUM.md   6,659 chars   the Loewdin tail          R 1373
    INDICES.md     12,695 chars   section IX, 13 indexes    R 1386
    PHYSICS.md      7,242 chars   Lambda_chem               R 1388

Not one exception -- a majority. And none announced itself: every build exited 0
and wrote a file that looked complete. REPRODUCTION confirms the build COMPLETES.
The whole finding is that completion is not the question.

    "An artefact called GENERATED that has a hand-edited region is not
     generated, and the claim that it cannot drift is exactly false there."

THE DANGEROUS FORM

physics.py writes its file IN PLACE rather than to stdout. Running it as a test
OVERWROTE the held copy and destroyed the authored section -- during the very
test being run to look for it. Recovered only because a restore point had been
cut twenty minutes earlier (R 1388).

So this protocol NEVER runs an in-place generator against the live artefact. It
copies the tree to a scratch directory first. That is not caution; it is the
recorded consequence of having done it the other way.

THE PROTOCOL

  1 DECLARE   Does the generator declare every region it does not write?
              A generator with an undeclared authored region fails here, before
              anything is run.

  2 ISOLATE   Never regenerate over the held copy. Copy the tree, or redirect to
              a temp path. If the generator writes in place and cannot be
              redirected, isolation is MANDATORY, not preferred.

  3 DIFF      Regenerate and compare against the held copy, normalising only the
              build date. Byte-identical or it does not round-trip.

  4 REFUSE    If the generator cannot produce its whole output, does it write
              NOTHING and exit non-zero? A generator that writes a partial file
              is worse than one that fails, because the partial file is believed.

Registers 1373, 1386, 1388. Companion to contingency.py (R 1383): both ask
whether a passing check could have failed.
"""
import os, re, shutil, subprocess, sys, tempfile

# generator -> (artefact, writes_to)  ·  "stdout" or "inplace"
GENERATORS = {
    "compendium.py":   ("COMPENDIUM.md", "stdout"),
    "indices.py":      ("INDICES.md",    "stdout"),
    "register_gen.py": ("REGISTER.md",   "stdout"),
    "physics.py":      ("PHYSICS.md",    "inplace"),
    "spectra.py":      ("SPECTRA.md",    "inplace"),
}
NORM = lambda s: re.sub(r"20\d\d-\d\d-\d\d", "DATE", s).strip()


def roundtrip(gen, artefact, mode, root=".", timeout=900):
    """Questions 2 and 3. Returns (ok, held_len, regen_len, note)."""
    held_path = os.path.join(root, artefact)
    if not os.path.exists(os.path.join(root, gen)):
        return None, 0, 0, "generator absent"
    held = open(held_path, encoding="utf-8").read()

    # QUESTION 2 — ISOLATE. An in-place writer is never run against the live tree.
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
        work = os.path.join(tmp, "w")
        shutil.copytree(root, work, ignore=shutil.ignore_patterns(
            ".zeno", "__pycache__", "*.tar.gz", "*.pdf"))
        try:
            r = subprocess.run([sys.executable, gen], cwd=work,
                               capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout)
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
            return False, len(held), 0, "TIMEOUT"
        if mode == "stdout":
            regen = r.stdout
        else:
            p = os.path.join(work, artefact)
            regen = open(p, encoding="utf-8").read() if os.path.exists(p) else ""
        ok = NORM(held) == NORM(regen)
        note = "" if ok else f"LOSS {len(held)-len(regen):+d} chars"
        if r.returncode != 0:
            note = (note + f" · exit {r.returncode}").strip(" ·")
        return ok, len(held), len(regen), note


def refuses_partial(gen, artefact, tail, root="."):
    """QUESTION 4. Hide the tail file; the generator must write NOTHING and
    exit non-zero rather than emit a lossy artefact."""
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
        work = os.path.join(tmp, "w")
        shutil.copytree(root, work, ignore=shutil.ignore_patterns(
            ".zeno", "__pycache__", "*.tar.gz", "*.pdf"))
        t = os.path.join(work, tail)
        if not os.path.exists(t): return None
        os.remove(t)
        before = open(os.path.join(work, artefact), encoding="utf-8").read()
        r = subprocess.run([sys.executable, gen], cwd=work,
                           capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=900)
        after = open(os.path.join(work, artefact), encoding="utf-8").read()
        return r.returncode != 0 and after == before


if __name__ == "__main__":
    root = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "."
    print("  ROUND-TRIP PROTOCOL — R 1373, 1386, 1388\n")
    print(f"  {'generator':<18}{'artefact':<16}{'writes':<10}"
          f"{'held':>8}{'regen':>8}  verdict")
    bad = 0
    for gen, (art, mode) in GENERATORS.items():
        ok, h, n, note = roundtrip(gen, art, mode, root)
        if ok is None:
            print(f"  {gen:<18}{art:<16}{mode:<10}{'—':>8}{'—':>8}  {note}")
            continue
        v = "round-trips" if ok else f"**FAILS** {note}"
        if not ok: bad += 1
        print(f"  {gen:<18}{art:<16}{mode:<10}{h:>8}{n:>8}  {v}")

    print("\n  QUESTION 4 — does the generator REFUSE to write a partial file?")
    for gen, art, tail in (("compendium.py", "COMPENDIUM.md", "COMPENDIUM-TAIL.md"),
                           ("indices.py",    "INDICES.md",    "INDICES-TAIL.md"),
                           ("physics.py",    "PHYSICS.md",    "PHYSICS-TAIL.md")):
        r = refuses_partial(gen, art, tail, root)
        if r is None:
            print(f"      {gen:<18} no tail file — nothing to withhold")
        elif r:
            print(f"      {gen:<18} REFUSES · writes nothing, exits non-zero")
        else:
            print(f"      {gen:<18} writes a LOSSY file when the tail is missing"
                  f"  ← acceptable only for a stdout writer, which cannot")
            print(f"      {'':<18}   destroy the held copy. In-place writers MUST refuse.")

    print(f"\n  {len(GENERATORS)-bad} of {len(GENERATORS)} round-trip.")
    raise SystemExit(1 if bad else 0)

**`roundtrip.py` built and registered as 1389.** Five of five round-trip. Gate passes, 165 to 1389.

Four questions: **DECLARE** — does the generator declare every region it doesn't write. **ISOLATE** — never regenerate over the held copy. **DIFF** — byte-identical once the build date is normalised. **REFUSE** — does it write nothing rather than a partial file.

Question 2 isn't caution, it's the recorded consequence of what I did an hour ago. The protocol copies the tree to a scratch directory and never touches the live one, so running it can't repeat that failure.

**And it failed its own first run**, which is the useful part. It reported `indices.py` losing fifteen characters — and the loss was real but wasn't content. `indices.py` prints its own progress *into* the artefact: the first line of INDICES.md reads *"measure every index: skipped, done in 0.4s"* one build and *"ok measure every index: 0.5s"* the next. Identical text, different elapsed time.

So a generated artefact whose first line varies with wall-clock time can never be byte-compared. I've normalised it in the protocol and queued the real repair as **F2c** — timing belongs on stderr, not in the file. That's a generator fault the test surfaced, not a test fault.

Question 4 also divided more cleanly than I expected when writing it. A stdout writer that produces a short file is harmless — the diff catches it and the held copy survives. An **in-place** writer must refuse, because it destroys the evidence while the test runs. `physics.py` refuses; `compendium.py` and `indices.py` don't, and correctly needn't.

Two protocols now sit together as a pair: `contingency.py` asks whether a check could have failed, `roundtrip.py` asks whether an artefact could have lost something. Same question, different objects.

F2b closed, F2c folded in. Item 5 next — Λ_ladder with the X-ray ladders.

If the 3p and 2p doublets were one object differing only by n, that ratio would be **0.2963 everywhere**. Instead it climbs steadily from 0.11 to 0.23 — a factor of two across the table, drifting toward the prediction without reaching it, and never flat.

**The identification fails.** The parameter-free prediction is off by a factor of roughly two, and — more damning — the observed ratio isn't constant at all.

| | Ca (20) | Kr (36) | Xe (54) | Yb (70) | Pb (82) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| observed 3p/2p | 0.108 | 0.145 | 0.193 | 0.216 | 0.226 |
| predicted, (2/3)³ | 0.2963 | 0.2963 | 0.2963 | 0.2963 | 0.2963 |

If the 3p and 2p doublets were one object differing only by n, that ratio would be **0.2963 everywhere**. Instead it climbs steadily from 0.11 to 0.23 — a factor of two across the table, drifting toward the prediction without reaching it, and never flat.

So the n⁻³ law does not carry the object from n = 2 to n = 3. **The core doublet and the valence-shell term structure are not one object at two depths.** Your hypothesis is refuted, cleanly and with no free parameter to blame.

Which means the PCA ambiguity does not dissolve. `valence·C` and `subvalence·A` stay two distinct cells, and the singleton rule stands: the index admits both and declines to choose.

Two things worth keeping from the failure.

**The drift has a shape and it points at screening, not relativity.** The ratio rises monotonically with Z toward 0.296 — approaching the hydrogenic value as the nucleus dominates and screening matters less. That's the right direction for a screening effect and the wrong one for a relativistic correction, which would push it past. So a single σ per element is the wrong model: the 2p and 3p electrons see *different* effective charges, and using the 2p's σ for the 3p is what breaks it. The identification might survive with σ(n), but a version needing a second fitted parameter per shell is a different and much weaker claim than the one tested.

**And Fe is anomalous** — obs/pred 1.635 where its neighbours sit near 0.45. The Z ≤ 60 scatter is sd 0.98 against a median 0.59, so the low-Z end is not just biased but wild. The L1M2/L1M3 pair carries `L1M2,3` blend flags across V through Ga, exactly that region. The theory column is unblended, but the pattern is suspicious enough that I'd not build on the light end without checking.

I've kept the capture — `XRAY-L1M.tsv`, 68 paired elements — since the 3p splitting is a real measurement regardless of what it refutes.

This wants registering as a refutation, and B2a's shared-cell question goes back to the queue unresolved rather than closed.

import csv, numpy as np
def load(p): return {(r["El"],r["A"]):r for r in csv.DictReader((l for l in open(p) if not l.startswith("#")),delimiter="\t")}
A3,A2=load("XRAY-KL3.tsv"),load("XRAY-KL2.tsv")
K=[k for k in A3 if k in A2 and A3[k]["grade"]=="M"]
d2={int(A3[k]["Z"]): float(A3[k]["E_theory_eV"])-float(A2[k]["E_theory_eV"]) for k in K}
R=[r for r in csv.DictReader((l for l in open("XRAY-L1M.tsv") if not l.startswith("#")),delimiter="\t")]
al=7.2973525693e-3; mc2=510998.95
C=lambda n: al**4*mc2/(2*n**3*2)
rows=[]
for r in R:
    z=int(r["Z"]); o3=float(r["split_3p"])
    if z not in d2 or o3<=0: continue
    s2=z-(d2[z]/C(2))**0.25
    s3=z-(o3/C(3))**0.25
    rows.append((z,r["El"],s2,s3,s3-s2))
print("  ONE STATEMENT:  dE = (Z - sigma(n,l))^4 · a^4 mc^2 / (2 n^3 l(l+1))")
print("  sigma extracted separately per shell. is the OFFSET constant?\n")
print(f"  {'el':>3}{'Z':>4}{'sigma_2p':>10}{'sigma_3p':>10}{'offset':>9}")
for z,el,s2,s3,d in rows:
    if z in (16,20,26,30,36,42,47,54,60,70,79,82):
        print(f"  {el:>3}{z:>4}{s2:>10.3f}{s3:>10.3f}{d:>9.3f}")
o=np.array([r[4] for r in rows]); Z=np.array([r[0] for r in rows])
lo=Z<=54
print(f"\n  offset sigma_3p - sigma_2p")
print(f"     all {len(o)} elements : mean {o.mean():>7.3f}  sd {o.std():.3f}")
print(f"     Z <= 54  ({lo.sum():>2})      : mean {o[lo].mean():>7.3f}  sd {o[lo].std():.3f}")
print(f"     Z >  54  ({(~lo).sum():>2})      : mean {o[~lo].mean():>7.3f}  sd {o[~lo].std():.3f}")
sl,ic=np.polyfit(Z,o,1)
print(f"     linear in Z: slope {sl:+.5f} per unit Z, intercept {ic:.3f}")
print(f"     -> the offset {'IS' if abs(sl)<0.005 else 'is NOT'} constant across the table")
# Slater's rules give a DERIVED offset. 2p sees 1s(hole:1)*0.85 + own-shell*0.35;

print(f"\n  SLATER'S RULES, no fitting: the extra screening a 3p sees over a 2p")

| region | Z | n | offset | sd |
|---|---|---|---|---|

Contingency-tested rather than eyeballed: the two largest deviations from the median, out of 53 elements, are Ti(22) and Sc(21). The probability of both landing on that adjacent pair by chance is **0.0007**.

And the discriminating check is the one that could have failed. **Z = 57, the 4f collapse, shows no break at all** — La sits at 5.292 against Ba's 5.296. If the offset broke at every Janet boundary it would be responding to something generic. It breaks at 3d and ignores 4f, which is exactly what a 3p electron should do: 3d is inside its screening region, 4f is outside it.

"""
THE SIX-PAIR SCREEN, applied.  Registers 1371, 1372; queue item C2.

The corridor refuted E = (N + 3/2) + beta*l(l+1) - alpha*<L.S> because the ratio
4 is an IDENTITY on intra-shell Delta-l = 2 spin-flip pairs, collapsing every one
of them to the single combination (4*beta + alpha) -- and the observed order holds
SIX such pairs, three demanding it positive and three negative.

Register 1372's screen: a candidate term gamma*T restores feasibility ONLY if
Delta-T is NON-DEGENERATE across those six pairs -- it must separate the three
demanding 4b+a > 0 from the three demanding 4b+a < 0. Six numbers, computed
before any fit.

The three candidates named in register 1370 and the queue:
  1. a WOODS-SAXON radial shape, whose n- and l-dependence no beta*l^2 captures
  2. a TENSOR term, spin-dependent and not captured by alpha*<L.S>
  3. an l-DEPENDENT EFFECTIVE MASS, changing the oscillator spacing itself

Each is reduced to what it contributes to a single-particle level, evaluated on
the six pairs, and tested for degeneracy. No fitting anywhere: the screen asks
whether the candidate CAN separate the groups, not how well it does.
"""
from fractions import Fraction as F
from math import sqrt

LCODE = {'s':0,'p':1,'d':2,'f':3,'g':4,'h':5,'i':6}

def parse(tag):
    n_r = int(tag[0]); ell = LCODE[tag[1]]
    num, den = tag[2:].split('/')
    return n_r, ell, F(int(num), int(den))

def level(tag):
    n_r, ell, j = parse(tag)
    N = 2*(n_r-1) + ell
    S = (j*(j+1) - ell*(ell+1) - F(3,4)) / 2
    return dict(tag=tag, n_r=n_r, ell=ell, j=j, N=N, S=S)

# the six degenerate pairs, from register 1371
PAIRS = [("2s1/2","1d3/2",  +1), ("2p3/2","1f5/2", +1), ("3p3/2","2f5/2", +1),
         ("2d3/2","3s1/2",  -1), ("1g7/2","2d5/2", -1), ("1h9/2","2f7/2", -1)]
#  +1 : the pair demands 4b + a > 0      -1 : demands 4b + a < 0

# ---- the candidate terms, each a function of a single-particle level --------
def woods_saxon(x):
    """A flattened-bottom well depresses high-l orbitals relative to the
    oscillator. The leading correction to the HO spectrum from a Woods-Saxon
    shape is a term in l(l+1) PLUS one in N(N+3) -- the surface diffuseness
    couples to the radial extent. Only the second is outside beta*l(l+1)."""
    return F(x['N']*(x['N']+3))

def tensor(x):
    """A tensor term contributes proportional to  <S12> , which for a single
    particle in a spin-orbit-coupled state reduces to a function of l and j:
      j = l+1/2 : -2(l-1)/(2l+3)      j = l-1/2 : -2(l+2)/(2l-1)
    (standard one-body reduction; zero for l = 0.)"""
    l = x['ell']
    if l == 0: return F(0)
    if x['j'] == l + F(1,2): return F(-2*(l-1), 2*l+3)
    return F(-2*(l+2), 2*l-1)

def eff_mass(x):
    """An l-dependent effective mass rescales the oscillator spacing itself, so
    the kinetic term (N + 3/2) is multiplied by a factor depending on l. The
    contribution beyond the plain HO is (N + 3/2)*l."""
    return F(2*x['N']+3, 2) * x['ell']

CANDIDATES = [("Woods-Saxon  N(N+3)", woods_saxon),
              ("tensor       <S12>",  tensor),
              ("eff. mass    (N+3/2)l", eff_mass),
              ("--- controls, must FAIL ---", None),
              ("l(l+1)  (already the beta slot)", lambda x: F(x['ell']*(x['ell']+1))),
              ("<L.S>   (already the alpha slot)", lambda x: x['S'])]

if __name__ == "__main__":
    print("  THE SIX-PAIR SCREEN (R 1372) — applied to the three candidates\n")
    print("  a candidate separates the groups iff the sign of gamma*dT can differ")
    print("  between the pairs demanding 4b+a > 0 and those demanding < 0.\n")
    for name, fn in CANDIDATES:
        if fn is None:
            print(f"\n  {name}\n"); continue
        dT_pos, dT_neg, row = [], [], []
        for a, b, sense in PAIRS:
            x, y = level(a), level(b)
            dT = fn(x) - fn(y)
            row.append(dT)
            (dT_pos if sense > 0 else dT_neg).append(dT)
        vals = " ".join(f"{str(v):>8}" for v in row)
        allsame = len(set(row)) == 1
        # non-degenerate iff some assignment of gamma makes the two groups differ
        sep = (max(dT_pos) < min(dT_neg)) or (max(dT_neg) < min(dT_pos))
        verdict = ("DEGENERATE — cannot separate" if allsame else
                   ("SEPARATES the two groups" if sep else
                    "overlapping — cannot separate by sign of gamma"))
        print(f"  {name:<34}{vals}")
        print(f"  {'':<34}  group + : {[str(v) for v in dT_pos]}")
        print(f"  {'':<34}  group - : {[str(v) for v in dT_neg]}")
        print(f"  {'':<34}  -> {verdict}\n")

import sys; sys.path.insert(0,"/home/claude/work")
from fractions import Fraction as F
from sixpair_screen import level, PAIRS, woods_saxon, tensor, eff_mass
import numpy as np

# The corridor constraint with a candidate term:
#     beta*dA + alpha*dS' + gamma*dT  <  0        (dN = 0 on all six)
# On these pairs dA = 4*dS', so the first two collapse to (4b+a)*dS'.
# Write s = 4b+a. Feasibility needs (s, gamma) with
#     dS'_i * s + dT_i * gamma < 0   for all six.
# That is a 2-D linear feasibility problem — SOLVE it, don't guess from signs.
def feasible(dS, dT):
    """is there (s, gamma) with dS_i*s + dT_i*gamma < 0 for every i?
    2-D homogeneous strict system: feasible iff the vectors (dS_i, dT_i) all lie
    strictly within some open half-plane."""
    V=[(float(a),float(b)) for a,b in zip(dS,dT)]
    for k in range(3600):
        th=k*np.pi/1800.0
        u=(np.cos(th),np.sin(th))
        if all(a*u[0]+b*u[1] < -1e-12 for a,b in V): return True,u
    return False,None

def deltas(fn):
    dS,dT=[],[]
    for a,b,_ in PAIRS:
        x,y=level(a),level(b)
        dS.append(y['S']-x['S'])
        dT.append(fn(x)-fn(y))
    return dS,dT

print("  THE SCREEN, DONE PROPERLY — 2-D linear feasibility, not sign-matching\n")

The Woods–Saxon result is the strongest and needs no fitting to see: **ΔT is exactly zero on every one of the six pairs.** Both members of each pair share the same oscillator shell N, so any term depending on N alone cancels identically. A flattened-bottom well shifts whole shells; the six binding constraints are all *within* a shell. The correction is invisible to them.

The other two separate the groups but still can't produce a feasible point, because separating isn't enough — the six vectors (ΔS′, ΔT) must lie strictly within one open half-plane, and they don't.

So register 1370's three named candidates are all eliminated, and the screen cost six numbers each rather than three fits. That is what 1372 was built to buy.

One thing I should flag rather than bury: my first version of the screen passed the controls when it should have failed them, because on these pairs Δ[ℓ(ℓ+1)] and Δ⟨L·S⟩ are proportional — which is the ratio-4 identity itself. Sign-matching was therefore guaranteed to succeed for anything correlated with the pair's own sense. The controls caught it. Without them I would have reported two candidates as viable.

### C.3. Nuclear shell model

The failure of the SEMF at reproducing the measured values of masses for light nuclei and nuclei with certain numbers of nucleons, the $magic\ numbers^9$ , led to the development of the $nuclear\ shell\ model$ by Goeppert-Mayer and Jensen (Nobel Prize in Physics, 1963). According to this model, protons and neutrons are seperately arranged in shells, and magic numbers occur when shells are filled. Nuclei with either Z or N (or both) equal to a magic (or doubly magic) number exhibit enhanced stability, and thus the $E_B$ spikes.

The various shell properties can be reproduced by approximating the nuclear potential with a three-dimensional harmonic oscillator plus a spin-orbit interaction. More advanced treatments include the usage of mean field potentials. However, a simple phenomenological term can be still be added to the SEMF and improve its performance.

In order to understand these magic numbers, starting from some simple models such as the square well or harmonic oscillator (HO) potential with analytical solutions, nuclear physicists tried to solve the corresponding Schrödinger equations. In 1949, independently, Haxel, Jensen, and Suess [1] and Mayer [2] introduced the spin-orbit (SO) potential which largely splits the states with high orbital angular momentum. In combination with the usual mean-field harmonic oscillator, square well, or Woods-Saxon potentials, the strong spin-orbit potential, although added by hand, excellently reproduces all traditional magic numbers in nuclear physics. Apart from the magic numbers, it also provides wonderful descriptions for nuclear ground-state and some low-lying excited-state properties.

Therefore, the substantial spin symmetry (SS) breaking between the spin doublets $(n, l, j = l \pm 1/2)$ is one of the most important concepts in nuclear structure.



The success of the nuclear shell model or spin-orbit potential is unprecedented. For light nuclei ( $A \lesssim 25$ ) the rotational features of nuclear spectra can be understood in a many-particle spherical shell-model framework in terms of the SU(3) coupling scheme of Elliott and Harvey [5–7]. By introducing the deformation-dependent oscillator length, Nilsson *et al.* [8, 9] extended the shell model to the deformed cases and built the foundation for describing not only the deformed nuclei but also nuclear rotation phenomena. Even nowadays, searching for new magic numbers and investigating shell structure evolution for unstable nuclei is still one of the key topics for the radioactive ion beam facilities worldwide [10].

#### IV. NUCLEAR STRUCTURE

The microscopic structure of atomic nuclei is described in terms of the spherical shell model [44–46], introduced in 1949 in order to explain the magic numbers 2, 8, 20, 28, 50, 82, 126, ..., at which nuclei present particularly stable configurations. The shell model is obtained from the three-dimensional isotropic harmonic oscillator, to which the spin-orbit interaction is added. It offers a satisfactory description of nuclei with few valence protons and valence neutrons outside closed shells, corresponding to the magic numbers, but it fails to explain the experimentally observed large nuclear quadrupole moments away from closed shells, where it has been suggested [47] in 1950 that spheroidal instead of spherical shapes lead to greater stability.

# I. INTRODUCTION

The nuclear shell model [1–5] is an appropriate tool for reproducing the observed magic numbers in atomic nuclei, which correspond to unusual stability of nuclei possessing these particular numbers of protons and/or neutrons. This model is based on the assumption that each nucleon is moving inside the nucleus in an average potential due to the other nucleons, resembling a threedimensional (3D) isotropic harmonic oscillator (HO) potential with a flattened bottom, to which the spin-orbit interaction is added, playing a crucial role in changing the 3D HO [6–8] magic numbers, 2, 8, 20, 40, 70, 112, ... into the nuclear magic numbers, 2, 8, 20, 28, 50, 82, 126, ..., observed experimentally. The single-particle energy levels, i.e., the nucleon energy levels within the 3D isotropic HO potential, are filled in accordance to the Pauli exclusion principle. Spherical coordinates are used for the description of the atomic nucleus.

## C. Spin-orbit and orbit-orbit interactions

The spin-orbit $(\mathbf{l} \cdot \mathbf{s})$ and orbit-orbit $(\mathbf{l}^2)$ interaction terms generate the necessary single-particle level splitting to obtain the correct schemes of the individual fragments after separation.

The use of deformation dependent form of these operators has been introduced in [16] for the Nilsson model and in [14] for the two center shell model; instead of the l operator one introduces:

$$\mathbf{l} = \frac{\nabla V \times \mathbf{p}}{m_0 \omega^2} \tag{31}$$

where V is the asymmetric two-center oscillator potential. The usual expression for the two operators are:

$$V(\mathbf{l} \cdot \mathbf{s}) = -2\kappa \hbar \omega \mathbf{l} \cdot \mathbf{s}$$

$$V(\mathbf{l}^2) = -\kappa \mu \hbar \omega \mathbf{l}^2.$$
(32)

Since one obtains the level schemes of two nuclei which lie in different mass regions, the strength parameters of the interactions $\kappa$ and $\mu$ will be different. 

The values we use for these parameters are:

$$\kappa_n = 0.0588 \quad \kappa_p = 0.0592$$

$$\mu_n = 0.328 \quad \mu_p = 0.335$$
(33)

for actinide region, and for light nuclei region:

$$\kappa_n = \kappa_p = 0.0601$$

$$\mu_n = \mu_p = 0.448.$$
(34)

Since the strength parameters are different for the asymmetric regions of the nuclear shape, they become z-dependent operators as follows:

$$\kappa \cdot \hbar \omega(z) = \kappa_1 \cdot \hbar \omega_1 + (\kappa_2 \cdot \hbar \omega_2 - \kappa_1 \cdot \hbar \omega_1) \Theta(z - z_0)$$

$$\kappa \mu \cdot \hbar \omega(z) = \kappa_1 \mu_1 \cdot \hbar \omega_1 + (\kappa_2 \mu_2 \cdot \hbar \omega_2 - \kappa_1 \mu_1 \cdot \hbar \omega_1) \Theta(z - z_0).$$
(35)

To obtain a Hermitian operator for $V(\mathbf{l} \cdot \mathbf{s})$ and $V(\mathbf{l}^2)$ one has to use the anticommutator [14]:

$$V(\mathbf{l} \cdot \mathbf{s}) = -\left[\kappa \cdot \hbar \omega(z), \frac{\nabla V \times \mathbf{p}}{m_0 \omega^2} \mathbf{s}\right],$$

## 3. Results and discussion

In this work, the deformation parameters $\varepsilon_2 = 0.217$ and $\varepsilon_4 = 0$ are taken from Ref. [78], which are chosen as an average of the neighboring even-even Hf and W isotopes. The Nilsson parameters ( $\kappa$ and $\mu$ ) are taken from Ref. [79], and a slight change of $\kappa_6$ (modified from 0.062 to 0.068) and $\mu_6$ (modified from 0.34 to 0.32) for neutron N=6 major shell is made. The neutron Nilsson parameters are changed to account for the observed ground state of <sup>167</sup>Hf. The Nilsson Hamiltonian, which is based on a harmonic oscillator with cylindrical symmetry to which a spin-orbit term and an angular momentum squared term are added, reads [32, 33]

$$H = H_0 - C\mathbf{l} \cdot \mathbf{s} - D(\mathbf{l}^2 - \langle \mathbf{l}^2 \rangle_N), \tag{1}$$

where $\mathbf{l}$ is the orbital angular momentum, $\mathbf{s}$ is the spin, C and D are parameters,

$$\langle \mathbf{l}^2 \rangle_N = \frac{1}{2} N(N+3) \tag{2}$$

is the average of the square of the orbital angular momentum within the $N{\rm th}$ oscillator shell, and

$$H_0 = -\frac{\hbar^2}{2M}\nabla^2 + \frac{M}{2}(\omega_x^2 x^2 + \omega_y^2 y^2 + \omega_z^2 z^2), \quad (3)$$

where x, y, z are the coordinates in the system fixed to the nucleus, $\omega_x$ , $\omega_y$ , $\omega_z$ are the harmonic oscillator angular frequencies along these axes, and M is the nuclear mass.

content.title: The deformed spin-orbit potential in Nilsson-model calculations - ScienceDirect
content.text:
A deformed spin-orbit potential of the Thomas form has been investigated in Nilsson-model calculations. Compared to the single-particle energy-level spacing, the level shifts due to deformation of the spin-orbit potential were found to be negligible for nuclei lighter than the rare earths. For the latter, however, the single-particle energies are shifted by up to 100 keV and re-ordering of some levels occurs. Single-particle energies in regions near the magic numbers 126 and 152 are shifted by up to 400 keV, showing that the spin-orbit deformation may be important in the prediction of stable super-heavy nuclei. The effect of the spin-orbit deformation on the single-particle wave function was found to be appreciable for all mass regions, the decoupling parameter, for example, changing by as much as 50 %. Magnetic moments calculated for rare-earth nuclei change by up to 20 %. ...



In this work, the set of eigenvectors common to the axially symmetrical deformed harmonic oscillator and to the third component of angular momentum, is used as a basis of representation (asymptotic basis). In this basis, the matrix elements of Nilsson's Hamiltonian are calculated by means of creation and destruction operators. A rather simple calculation gives, after a diagonalisation, level diagrams as a function of deformation. The influence of various corrective terms, used instead of l2 and l · s (particularly lT Nilsson's term) is discussed. Within the framework of these approaches and in order to test them, we calculate total energy as a function of deformation for some nuclei. content.text:
#### 1.2.3 The deformed shell model

As was mentioned above, the spherical Shell Model has difficulies when dealing with issues regarding deformed nuclei. Therefore, the deformed shell model was introduced.

The modified harmonic oscillator potential, *i.e.*, Nilsson potential [8], allows to take deformation into account. The Hamiltonian in this case can be written as:

$$H_{Nilsson} = \frac{-\hbar^2}{2m} \nabla^2 + \frac{m}{2} \left( \omega_x^2 x^2 + \omega_y^2 y^2 + \omega_z^2 z^2 \right) - 2\kappa \hbar \omega_0 \left[ \vec{l} \cdot \vec{s} - \mu \left( l^2 - \langle l^2 \rangle_N \right) \right], \tag{1.13}$$

where the $(\vec{l} \cdot \vec{s})$ term represents the spin-orbit force, and the $(l^2 - \langle l^2 \rangle_N)$ term was introduced by Nilsson to simulate the flattening of the nuclear potential at the bottom of the well (as obtained with a WS potential). The factors $\kappa$ and

 $\mu$ determine the strength of the spin-orbit and $l^2$ term, respectively.

#### 4. Results and discussion

It is well known that the traditional parameters ( $\kappa$ and $\mu$ ) [41] used in the Nilsson Hamiltonian have been quite successful in describing the single-particle structure for stable nuclei, especially for those in the rare-earth and the actinide region. However, for the specific nucleus, this level scheme is unable to correctly reproduce the experimental bandhead energies of the low-lying excited 1-quasiparticle bands, which is very important for investigating the rotational properties of these nuclei, e.g., the level crossing frequencies et al. To illustrated this more obviously, the experimental and the calculated bandhead energies of 1-quasiparticle bands in <sup>159</sup>Ho are shown in Tab. 1. The calculated results using traditional Nilsson parameters [41] and the modified values are denoted by $E_{\rm Cal}^{\rm Lund}$ and $E_{\rm Cal}^{\rm New}$ , respectively. 

It can be seen that the calculated 1-quasiparticle excitation energies using Lund systematics are much higher than the experimental values. After slightly adjusting the Nilsson parameters (see Sec. 3),

all the calculated results are lowered about 200 keV and are more consistent with the data except $5/2^+[402]$ , whose excitation energy is still higher than the experimental value. If the Nilsson parameters ( $\kappa$ and $\mu$ ) were adjusted more sophisticated, the calculated results may be improved further. content.title: Deformed Harmonic Oscillators for Metal Clusters: Analytic Properties   and Supershells
content.text:
#### 2. Nilsson's Modified Oscillator (MO)

The potential of the Modified Oscillator (MO) introduced in nuclear physics by Nilsson [7, 8] (with the spin-orbit term omitted) is

$$V = \frac{1}{2}\hbar\omega\rho^2 - \hbar\omega\mu'(\mathbf{L}^2 - \langle \mathbf{L}^2 \rangle_n), \qquad \rho = r\sqrt{\frac{M\omega}{\hbar}}, \tag{1}$$

where

$$\langle \mathbf{L}^2 \rangle_n = \frac{n(n+3)}{2}.\tag{2}$$

The effect of the $\mathbf{L}^2$ term is to flatten the bottom of the potential. In addition it causes an overall compression of the spectrum, which is avoided through the addition of the $\langle \mathbf{L}^2 \rangle_n$ term, which will be further discussed later.

The energy eigenvalues of Nilsson's modified harmonic oscillator are [7, 8]

$$E_{nl} = \hbar\omega \left(n + \frac{3}{2}\right) - \hbar\omega\mu' \left(l(l+1) - \frac{1}{2}n(n+3)\right),\tag{3}$$

"""
Lambda_merged -- (Z, c, n, l, 2S+1), the index register 1341 names and no script
ever built. Queue item A2.

WHY IT EXISTS

Lambda_spectra is the only index of the fourteen that stays open, and 1341 names
the cause: it has no PRINCIPAL QUANTUM NUMBER. Its cells are (Z, charge, l,
multiplicity) -- a channel, with n running inside it. The walk supplies n,
because a is defined per subshell, and a = delta/sqrt(p) makes them one object.

    Lambda_spectra   (Z, c, l, 2S+1)      328 channels     n absent
    the walk         per element          106 steps        n present
    MERGED           (Z, c, n, l, 2S+1)   cells are (species, subshell)

1341 predicts 1,195 cells for the 108 neutrals. That figure is TESTED here, not
assumed -- it is a count over the observed ground configurations, so it can come
out wrong.

WHAT IS AND IS NOT ASKED

E is computed in the SUBJECT'S OWN ORDER, not minimised over permutations. Z has
one order (the nuclear charge), n and l have theirs (the quantum numbers), and
2S+1 has its own. A.erel is explicit that E = 0 is a statement about a
COORDINATISATION, and that any composite cell count has SOME relabelling in which
it vanishes -- so a minimised E here would be meaningless. The coordinates come
from the subject.
"""
import re, sys
from itertools import product

LSYM = "spdfghi"

def read_ground():
    """the 108 observed ground configurations, from ground.py's own table."""
    src = open("ground.py", encoding="utf-8").read()
    rows = re.findall(r'\(\s*(\d+)\s*,\s*"([A-Za-z]+)"\s*,\s*"([^"]+)"', src)
    if not rows:
        rows = re.findall(r'^\s*(\d+)\s*:\s*"([^"]*)"', src, re.M)
        rows = [(z, "", c) for z, c in rows]
    return rows

def subshells(cfg):
    """expand a configuration string into (n, l, occ) triples."""
    NOBLE = {"[He]":"1s2", "[Ne]":"1s2.2s2.2p6",
             "[Ar]":"1s2.2s2.2p6.3s2.3p6",
             "[Kr]":"1s2.2s2.2p6.3s2.3p6.3d10.4s2.4p6",
             "[Xe]":"1s2.2s2.2p6.3s2.3p6.3d10.4s2.4p6.4d10.5s2.5p6",
             "[Rn]":"1s2.2s2.2p6.3s2.3p6.3d10.4s2.4p6.4d10.5s2.5p6.4f14.5d10.6s2.6p6"}
    for k, v in NOBLE.items():
        cfg = cfg.replace(k, v)
    out = []
    for tok in re.findall(r'(\d)([spdfghi])(\d*)', cfg):
        n, l, k = int(tok[0]), LSYM.index(tok[1]), int(tok[2] or 1)
        out.append((n, l, k))
    return out

def opR(X, d):
    X = set(X); vals = [sorted({x[i] for x in X}) for i in range(d)]
    def env(i, j):
        m = {}

"""
Lambda_merged -- (Z, c, n, l, 2S+1), the index register 1341 names and no script
ever built. Queue item A2.

WHY IT EXISTS

Lambda_spectra is the only index of the fourteen that stays open, and 1341 names
the cause: it has no PRINCIPAL QUANTUM NUMBER. Its cells are (Z, charge, l,
multiplicity) -- a channel, with n running inside it. The walk supplies n,
because a is defined per subshell, and a = delta/sqrt(p) makes them one object.

    Lambda_spectra   (Z, c, l, 2S+1)      328 channels     n absent
    the walk         per element          106 steps        n present
    MERGED           (Z, c, n, l, 2S+1)   cells are (species, subshell)

1341 predicts 1,195 cells for the 108 neutrals. That figure is TESTED here, not
assumed -- it is a count over the observed ground configurations, so it can come
out wrong.

WHAT IS AND IS NOT ASKED

E is computed in the SUBJECT'S OWN ORDER, not minimised over permutations. Z has
one order (the nuclear charge), n and l have theirs (the quantum numbers), and
2S+1 has its own. A.erel is explicit that E = 0 is a statement about a
COORDINATISATION, and that any composite cell count has SOME relabelling in which
it vanishes -- so a minimised E here would be meaningless. The coordinates come
from the subject.
"""
import re, sys
from itertools import product

LSYM = "spdfghi"

def read_ground():
    """the 108 observed ground configurations, from ground.py's own table."""
    src = open("ground.py", encoding="utf-8").read()
    rows = re.findall(r'\(\s*(\d+)\s*,\s*"([A-Za-z]+)"\s*,\s*"([^"]+)"', src)
    if not rows:
        rows = re.findall(r'^\s*(\d+)\s*:\s*"([^"]*)"', src, re.M)
        rows = [(z, "", c) for z, c in rows]
    return rows

def subshells(cfg):
    """expand a configuration string into (n, l, occ) triples."""
    NOBLE = {"[He]":"1s2", "[Ne]":"1s2.2s2.2p6",
             "[Ar]":"1s2.2s2.2p6.3s2.3p6",
             "[Kr]":"1s2.2s2.2p6.3s2.3p6.3d10.4s2.4p6",
             "[Xe]":"1s2.2s2.2p6.3s2.3p6.3d10.4s2.4p6.4d10.5s2.5p6",
             "[Rn]":"1s2.2s2.2p6.3s2.3p6.3d10.4s2.4p6.4d10.5s2.5p6.4f14.5d10.6s2.6p6"}
    for k, v in NOBLE.items():
        cfg = cfg.replace(k, v)
    out = []
    for tok in re.findall(r'(\d)([spdfghi])(\d*)', cfg):
        n, l, k = int(tok[0]), LSYM.index(tok[1]), int(tok[2] or 1)
        out.append((n, l, k))
    return out

def opR(X, d):
    X = set(X); vals = [sorted({x[i] for x in X}) for i in range(d)]
    def env(i, j):
        m = {}
        for x in X: m[x[j]] = max(m.get(x[j], -10**9), x[i])
        b, o = -10**9, {}
        for t in sorted(m): b = max(b, m[t]); o[t] = b
        return o
    phi = {(i, j): env(i, j) for i in range(d) for j in range(d) if i != j}
    return {x for x in product(*vals)
            if all(x[i] <= phi[(i,j)][x[j]] for i in range(d) for j in range(d) if i != j)}

if __name__ == "__main__":
    rows = read_ground()
    print(f"  ground configurations read: {len(rows)}")
    cells, per_z = set(), {}
    for z, sym, cfg in rows:
        z = int(z)
        ss = subshells(cfg)
        per_z[z] = len(ss)
        for n, l, k in ss:
            # 2S+1 for a subshell holding k of its 2(2l+1): Hund's first rule
            cap = 2*(2*l+1)
            unpaired = min(k, cap - k) if k > cap//2 else min(k, cap//2)
            cells.add((z, 1, n, l, unpaired + 1))
    print(f"  cells (Z, c, n, l, 2S+1) : {len(cells)}")
    print(f"  register 1341 predicts   : 1195   -> "
          f"{'MATCHES' if len(cells)==1195 else 'DIFFERS by %+d' % (len(cells)-1195)}")
    print(f"  subshells per element: min {min(per_z.values())} "
          f"max {max(per_z.values())} mean {sum(per_z.values())/len(per_z):.1f}")

    # c is constant at 1 across the neutrals, so it is a DEFINING LETTER (A.define)
    # and contributes no envelope. Drop it and index on the four that vary.
    X = {(z, n, l, m) for z, c, n, l, m in cells}
    box = 1
    for i in range(4): box *= len({x[i] for x in X})
    print(f"\n  c is constant at 1 over the neutrals — a DEFINING LETTER (A.define),")
    print(f"  contributing no envelope. Indexing on (Z, n, l, 2S+1).")
    print(f"      cells {len(X)} · box {box} · density {len(X)/box:.4f}")
    R = opR(X, 4)
    print(f"      |ℛ(X)| = {len(R)}   E = {len(R)-len(X)}")

content.text:
Built, and it does **not** close — E = 10,840 on 1,083 cells. Two things need saying honestly, and the second matters more than the first.

**Register 1341's count is wrong.** It predicts 1,195 cells; the construction from the 108 observed ground configurations gives **1,083**, short by 112. My count could be at fault, but it's a direct enumeration of subshells with 2S+1 read from the observed term, so the discrepancy needs resolving rather than splitting. Worth noting the shape: 108 elements at a mean of 10.2 subshells gives 1,100, so 1,083 is the right order and 1,195 would need 11.1 per element.

    the subshell   (n, l, k)       Lambda's own source triple

c and Ne vary independently of Z -- must change E. That is a falsifiable

from itertools import product

NOBLE = {"[He]":"1s2", "[Ne]":"1s2 2s2 2p6",
         "[Ar]":"1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2 3p6",
         "[Kr]":"1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2 3p6 3d10 4s2 4p6",
         "[Xe]":"1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2 3p6 3d10 4s2 4p6 4d10 5s2 5p6",
         "[Cd]":"1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2 3p6 3d10 4s2 4p6 4d10 5s2",
         "[Hg]":"1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2 3p6 3d10 4s2 4p6 4d10 5s2 5p6 4f14 5d10 6s2",
         "[Rn]":"1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2 3p6 3d10 4s2 4p6 4d10 5s2 5p6 4f14 5d10 6s2 6p6"}

def subshells(cfg):
    for k, v in NOBLE.items(): cfg = cfg.replace(k, v)

    return [(int(a), LSYM.index(b), int(c or 1))

        Ne = Z - int(f[2])

    print("  Λ_merged AS TWO TRIPLES — (Z, c, Nₑ) × (n, ℓ, k)\n")
    e1 = report("the 108 NEUTRALS alone", neutral, N)
    print()
    e2 = report("the H-Ar I-III capture alone (ions included)", ions, N)
    print()
    e3 = report("BOTH", neutral | ions, N)

    print("\n  THE PREDICTION: ions make c and Nₑ vary independently of Z,")
    print("  so the species triple stops being rank one.")
    print(f"      neutrals only : E = {e1}")
    print(f"      with ions     : E = {e3}")

The routing fails, and it fails cleanly enough to be worth keeping.

**Only 3 of 12 land on a half or full shell — and the ordinary steps do it more often, 38%.** So the exchange explanation is not merely unproven, it runs the wrong way: the anomalous steps reach half or full occupancy *less* than the normal ones. Cr, Cu and Pd are the textbook cases and they're the whole of it; Nb at 4d⁴, Ru at 4d⁷, Pt at 5d⁹, Pa at 5f², Rf at 6d² reach nothing special at all.

So the story I told two messages ago — *the walk overshoots to reach a closed or half-closed shell* — covers a quarter of the departures and I generalised it from the famous examples. That's the same error as the six-and-five split earlier: describing outcomes and calling them mechanisms.

Contingency again. The check I ran had a base rate available and I didn't compute it until now; against 38% baseline, 25% is evidence *against*.

What survives is the derivation, which doesn't depend on any of this: **rival = donor if and only if the donor is not full**, 12 of 12, from Pauli admissibility alone. That stands because it was tested against a condition that could have failed, and Pd is its own control.

What's refuted is my proposed *cause*. The corridor's preference for a full-donor configuration is not exchange reaching a stable shell. Λ_chem's routing rule says to name the property and the class before calling a residual unexplained — I named exchange, the class predicted a signature, and the signature isn't there.

So the residual returns to the queue genuinely open, with one candidate eliminated by measurement rather than by argument. That's worth more than the wrong mechanism would have been.

    pr={(n,l):o for n,l,o in G.expand(Z-1)}
    cu={(n,l):o for n,l,o in G.expand(Z)}
    got=[k for k in cu if cu[k]>pr.get(k,0)][0]
    lost=[k for k in pr if pr[k]>cu.get(k,0)]

    for n,l in cand:
        if (n,l)==(gn,gl): continue
        rp=n-l-1; d=math.sqrt(rp)-math.sqrt(gp)
        if abs(d)<1e-12: continue
        if d>0 and (n-gn)/d<hi: hi,bhi=(n-gn)/d,(n,l)
        if d<0 and (n-gn)/d>lo: lo,blo=(n-gn)/d,(n,l)

The 1/cap scaling holds in order but not in ratio: **1.000, 0.437, 0.279, 0.204** against the naive 1, 0.33, 0.20, 0.14. So the cap is the leading factor and not the whole of it — √rad_r and the squared gap both move with cap and soften it. That's stated in the script rather than glossed.

The pull is largest at **s with p_r = 3, −0.176**, and that is the case that governs the 4d row: Mo, Rh and Pd are bound by 5s, which has p = 5−0−1 = 4 in the empty case and drops as it fills. One electron in that 5s draws the ceiling down by roughly a tenth to two tenths of a unit — which is the whole of the margin difference between Mo and Pd.

So the chain from your question is now closed end to end, and every link is arithmetic:

**Pauli** decides which rival can bind — a full subshell is inadmissible, so 5s at two is excluded and 5p binds; 5s at one is admissible and binds instead.
**The cap** decides how hard that rival pulls — s divides by two, so its single electron moves the ceiling most.
**The gap** squares the effect as the radicands approach.

Together they contract the corridor at exactly Mo and Rh, and leave Pd's alone. No fitted term anywhere: cap, node count, and occupancy are all counts.

Saved as `rival_pull.py`, with the degenerate case handled explicitly rather than crashing — a rival with rad_r = rad_g imposes no bound at all, which is not a singularity but a rival that cannot be ordered against the entrant at any *a*.

I'd register this now: the mechanism, its algebra, and the honest note that 1/cap is leading-order rather than exact.

**Monotone ascent is impossible**, and the obstruction is exact and structural rather than incidental.

It fails at **Z = 58, cerium** — the 4f block opening — and stays failed for the entire lanthanide run, Ce through Yb. Every one of those corridors has a **ceiling of 0.7071 = 1/√2 with no floor at all**, while *a* has already climbed to 1.2168 at caesium. Then it fails again at Pa and U in the 5f block, ceiling 1.3660 against *a* at 1.3938.

So the descents in the record aren't errors. The f blocks *demand* them. Cs pushes *a* to 1.2168 and the 4f opening at Ce requires *a* below 0.7071 — the recorded value at La is exactly 0.7071, which is that ceiling.

And the global statement is decisive: **the highest floor anywhere is 1.9841 and the tightest ceiling anywhere is 0.7071.** The floor exceeds the ceiling, so no single *a* serves the whole table by any margin at all — which is register 1341's *necessity of state* proved rather than asserted, and proved in the strongest form: not merely that one value fails, but that the constraint set is globally infeasible by a factor of nearly three.

So your instinct that ascent should be the natural order is right about *most* of the walk — *a* does climb, 0.5774 → 1.0000 → 1.2168 — and it's the **f blocks that break it**. Both descents in the record are f-block openings, at 4f and 5f. Nowhere else.

That's a much smaller statement than "the update rule is undetermined." The rule is: **ascend, except that an f opening forces a descent.** Two exceptions in 106 steps, both at the same structural position, and Q.collapse already fixes those thresholds at Z = 57 and 89.

That fails, and not marginally — the predicted δ is between 0 and 0.55 of measured, with a median ratio of 0.18. Three elements predict exactly zero against measured defects of 0.40, 0.73 and 1.60.

So **a = δ/√p does not hold as I applied it**, and I should say plainly which part is mine rather than the record's. Register 1341 states the relation; what I supplied was the identification — that the *a* carried by the walk at element Z is the *a* of the channel (Z, ℓ) of that element's entering subshell. Nothing in 1341 says that. It says a lives in the walk *per element* and δ lives in Λ_spectra *per channel*, and calls the merge "the first index whose cells are (species, subshell)". The merge is the claim that they share an index, not that one number equals the other.

And the failure has structure worth keeping. The three zeros are elements where the entering subshell is node-free after the block opening set *a* = 0 — so δ_pred = 0·√p = 0 regardless of p. That's the *a* = 0 placement, not the relation. Where *a* is non-zero the ratio runs 0.36 to 0.55, so the prediction is consistently *low* by roughly a factor of two to three rather than randomly wrong.

Which points somewhere specific: **the measured δ is δ₀ for a Rydberg channel**, an outer electron far from the core, while the walk's *a* governs which subshell the *last bound* electron enters. Those are different electrons in different regimes, and Λ_ryd already records that a channel's δ is a convergent sequence — Cd I's ns runs 3.7171 down to 3.6610 — not one number.

So the trajectory's role in the Löwdin completion isn't δ = a√p. The link exists as an index merge, and the numeric identification is mine and wrong. I'd want to read register 1341's antecedents before proposing another form.
